clock_quality.rule: published rows carry the authority's stated release instant in release_utc (converted from local_tz); unvintaged rows (holidays, OPEC meetings, one EIA slip, and the central-bank and Indian releases whose authority states no clock) carry only a civil date in release_date with release_utc null and are excluded from point-in-time reads; rows built from a standing rule for future weeks say so in notes

columns.meaning: coarse grouping: labor, inflation, growth, fed, central_bank, rates, energy, positioning, china, activity, holiday
columns.name: event_family

columns.meaning: civil date of the release in local_tz
columns.name: release_date

columns.meaning: scheduled release instant in UTC; null when the authority states no clock
columns.name: release_utc

columns.meaning: the same instant as a naive wall-clock time in local_tz
columns.name: release_local

columns.meaning: IANA zone of the authority (America/New_York, Asia/Shanghai, Asia/Tokyo, Asia/Kolkata, Europe/London, Europe/Berlin, Europe/Vienna)
columns.name: local_tz

columns.meaning: who states the schedule; 'secondary' marks rows taken from a calendar provider instead
columns.name: authority

columns.meaning: period the release covers: YYYY-MM, YYYY-Qn, a week-ending date, an FOMC meeting label
columns.name: period_ref

columns.meaning: page or file the row was parsed from (Wayback URLs for archived years)
columns.name: source_url

columns.meaning: raw capture of that source under build/calendar/, listed in raw/INDEX.csv
columns.name: capture_path

columns.meaning: published: release_utc is the source's stated instant; unvintaged: civil date only, release_utc null
columns.name: clock_quality

columns.meaning: how the date and clock were established, plus any caveat
columns.name: notes

conventions: release_utc is the authority's stated instant converted from local_tz; rows built from a standing rule (future weeks) say so in notes
holidays are civil days with release_utc null
FOMC press conferences use the Fed's standing 2:30 p.m. ET slot; statements and minutes carry the clock stated on the meeting page where available
secondary_authorities: Investing.com economic calendar (secondary; ISM's site is gated by reCAPTCHA/SSO with no archived schedule)
Investing.com economic calendar (secondary; S&P Global's release page lists only upcoming months)
